clue.text: He may be responsible for a stickup on board

definitions.text: He may be responsible for a stickup on board

parts.words: He may be responsible for a stickup on board
parts.note: a stickup sounds like an armed robbery, but here it is a notice pasted up on a hoarding or board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stickup' suggests a hold-up; the board is a hoarding where notices are pasted.
explanation.definitionFit: This person's job is pasting advertising notices onto walls and hoardings.

clue.text: Eat hurriedly and run for it

explanation.definitionFit: To gobble food is one sense; to dash away in flight, as a horse does, is the other.

clue.text: Artist adopting provincial girl as permitted by law

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the artist's name holds the girl inside it

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely, the Restoration portrait painter
gal is a dialect or folksy word for a girl

explanation.surface: A painter takes in a country girl as his ward, all above board.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lawfully means doing it within what the statutes allow.

clue.text: Interfere in a row?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meddling uninvited; literally it is what a rower does, adding a blade to the rowing.

clue.text: One travelling free to Washington, being in government

indicators.note: these words place the short pieces within the word for government

parts.note: sway means rule or dominion
taken as written
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: Someone gets a free trip to the American capital by holding office.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden passenger on a ship or plane rides without paying a fare.

clue.text: Guarantee being seen wandering around the old city

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the old city
letters that wander move about, so the word seen is jumbled

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A pledge made while seen strolling around an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns SEEN into ENSE, and 'around' puts that round UR.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to secure or warrant it.

clue.text: Community's initial rejection of pub sign

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word community is taken
rejecting throws back, so the word for pub is read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A village rejects the board hung outside its local inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns BAR into RAB; the sign is a zodiac sign, Cancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer, the fourth sign of the zodiac, is symbolised by this crustacean.

clue.text: Denial of judge over American gangster

indicators.note: in a down clue the referee's letters sit above the rest

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A judge turns down a request from an American mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to a request is a rejection of it.

clue.text: Grain from Indonesian island, say, held up by naval commander

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of, held up by, the second
say signals that we want a word that sounds like the island's name

parts.note: Bali is an island in Indonesia
CO is commanding officer
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Grain shipped from Bali is propped up by a ship's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BARLEY sounds like BALI.
explanation.definitionFit: A single seed of a cereal crop is a grain; the term also names the spirit of malt liquor.

clue.text: It may have a keeper supplying easily digested game

parts.note: light food is easy on the stomach
house is another name for the game of bingo or housey-housey

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's supply of meat that is easy on the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeper' and 'game' suggest a gamekeeper; the keeper tends the lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal beacon tower was traditionally staffed by a resident keeper who tended the lamp.

clue.text: Note received by a king at a great distance

indicators.note: being received by means taken inside, so the a-and-king pair hold the note

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A monarch receives a message from far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far off is located a long way away.

clue.text: Morality play character with money for all the people

parts.note: Everyman is the hero of the medieval morality play of that name
jack is slang for money, as in 'not worth jack'

explanation.surface: A character from a medieval play hands out cash to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means every single individual, each and every one.

clue.text: Most of a cut of beef in a pastry case

indicators.note: the final letter of the beef cut is dropped, leaving most of it

parts.note: flank is a cut from the side of a cow

explanation.surface: A piece of beef baked in a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: An open tart with a pastry base and a filling, sweet or savoury.

clue.text: A striver? One may be a ruthless self-seeker!

indicators.note: a striver and one may be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone striving hard may turn out to be an unscrupulous climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals rearranging A STRIVER with I.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart who pushes ambitiously for status and wealth, without scruples.

clue.text: Composer almost devoured by blighter's dog!

indicators.note: being devoured means being swallowed inside the word for blighter

parts.note: a rotter is a blighter, a cad; the possessive 's is no letter

indicators.note: the last letter of the composer's name is left off

parts.note: Kurt Weill, composer of The Threepenny Opera

explanation.surface: A composer is nearly eaten by a scoundrel's fierce hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims WEILL to WEIL, which goes inside ROTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A German breed of large, powerful guard animal.

clue.text: Like the ramblings of a synod about Galilee, for instance?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned round and rearranged

parts.note: the Sea of Galilee is an example of a sea

explanation.surface: A church council's long-winded talk about the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SYNOD with SEA (Galilee is a sea).
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Odysseus, whose ten-year voyage home was a byword for long wandering.

clue.text: Gaiety's cheerful play

explanation.definitionFit: The word means merriment or fun as a noun and a lively romp as an activity.

clue.text: Unite in concern shown by the church about drinks

parts.note: a concern is a business, company, abbreviated CO
ales are beers
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A business backed by the church gets people together over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse or come together into one mass or body.

clue.text: Hard worker given a horse

explanation.definitionFit: To work like a determined toiler is to labour hard; the Greeks gave the people of Troy a wooden horse.

clue.text: Noisome, like comparisons, Dogberry said

explanation.definitionFit: Smelly or stinking is the first sense; Shakespeare's constable Dogberry in Much Ado says 'comparisons are odorous', mangling odious.

clue.text: Daily traveller involved in exchange?

explanation.definitionFit: One travels into work every day; to commute also means to exchange or swap one thing for another.

clue.text: Republic initially investing substantial income in fish

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: the opening letters of three words are taken

explanation.surface: A state that starts out putting big earnings into seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African state whose capital is Tunis.

clue.text: Woman doctor restricted by a miserly cut-back

indicators.note: restricted means confined, so the doctor is held inside
the back, the final letter, of the word for miserly is cut off

parts.note: near means stingy

explanation.surface: A female medic is hemmed in by stingy budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' trims NEAR to NEA; with A in front, it holds DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, as in the female names section of a list.

clue.text: Proposal accepted by eastern fellow showing strong feelings

indicators.note: being accepted means taken in, so the eastern fellow holds the proposal

parts.note: Al, a man's name, stands for any fellow
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A man from the east is moved when his offer is accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred, tearful or passionate is displaying deep feeling.

clue.text: A figure from Loughton, in Essex

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the place names

explanation.surface: A statistic about a town in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Loughton is a town in Essex, the county north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit or number, one more than eight.

clue.text: Irritation in the bar

explanation.definitionFit: Worry or agitation is one sense; a raised ridge on a guitar fingerboard is the other.

clue.text: Branch line constructed in the backwater

indicators.note: back means the word for water is read from end to start

parts.note: a pool is a body of water

explanation.surface: A railway spur built in a sleepy rural backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwater' splits into 'back' (read backwards) and 'water', a POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail track that leaves the main line and rejoins it farther on.

clue.text: Bath in lock with hesitation? One shouldn't be there

indicators.note: the bath goes inside the lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a bath, a place for bathing
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly bathing in a canal lock is where they ought not to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is also an English spa town, which helps hide the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters private land unlawfully is somewhere forbidden.

clue.text: Sudden demand for the first prints

explanation.definitionFit: A surge of requests is one sense; in film the first unedited prints of a day's shooting are called this.

clue.text: A ruse a Turk developed to get pickled cabbage

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Turk hatches a scheme to obtain preserved cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: The German dish of finely shredded fermented cabbage.
